titulo: The Hotel That Rose With the Guests Inside

lineas.texto: [excited, storytelling hook] In 1861, Chicago lifted a giant brick hotel SIX FEET into the air... [incredulous, building] with the guests STILL INSIDE.
[conspiratorial, fast] You see, Chicago was built on a swamp. [disgusted, comedic] Wagons sank. Horses got stuck. [chuckling] And legend says someone put up a sign: [deadpan] "No bottom here."
[mock-serious, rapid] So the city decided to bury its own streets: [building] new sewers on top... [astonished] then up to FOURTEEN feet of dirt!
[ironic, slowing down] Which left the fanciest hotel in town... [deadpan, comedic] sitting in a hole.
[thinking aloud, quick] Tear it down? [scoffs] Too expensive. Lift it? [laughing mockingly] Everybody laughed. [mocking voice] "It's solid BRICK!"
[mysterious, confident] Then a young building mover named George Pullman said, [smug, calm, cool] "I'll lift it. Your guests won't feel a thing."
[intense, big reveal] He filled trenches under the hotel with FIVE HUNDRED men... [awed] and a THOUSAND jackscrews.
[tense whisper] On a signal... [sharp, commanding] every man gave his screw a tiny turn, all at once, [suspenseful, slow] and the whole hotel rose... [whispers] a hair.
[rhythmic, punchy, building energy] Turn. Rise. Wedge in timber. [excited, faster] Again and again!
[light, amused] Upstairs, guests ate, slept and checked out like nothing was happening. [laughing] Even a U.S. Senator.
[triumphant] Six feet later, the hotel sat LEVEL with the new street, [proud, warm] and nobody inside felt a thing.
[sly pause] Well... almost. [amused, playful] Every morning, the front steps were a little bit taller.
